# Resource: stripe_billing_alert

Notifies you when the usage a billing meter records crosses a threshold. `terraform destroy` deactivates the alert, because Stripe cannot delete one; it stays in the Stripe account. Stripe does not update alerts, so every argument except `status` forces replacement. `status` can be set to `active`, `inactive` or `archived`; an archived alert never triggers or activates again.

~> Stripe cannot deactivate an archived alert, because archiving one is final. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace it, fail at plan time for such a billing alert. To stop managing one, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_billing_meter" "api_calls" {
  display_name = "API calls"
  event_name   = "api_call"

  default_aggregation = {
    formula = "sum"
  }

  customer_mapping = {
    type              = "by_id"
    event_payload_key = "stripe_customer_id"
  }

  value_settings = {
    event_payload_key = "value"
  }
}

resource "stripe_billing_alert" "heavy_usage" {
  alert_type = "usage_threshold"
  title      = "API calls above 1000"

  usage_threshold = {
    gte        = 1000
    meter      = stripe_billing_meter.api_calls.id
    recurrence = "one_time"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `alert_type` - (Required) The type of alert to create. Possible values: `usage_threshold`. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `title` - (Required) The title of the alert. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `status` - (Optional) Status of the alert. This can be active, inactive or archived. Possible values: `active`, `inactive`, `archived`.
* `usage_threshold` - (Optional) The configuration of the usage threshold. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`usage_threshold`](#usage_threshold) below.

<a id="usage_threshold"></a>
### `usage_threshold`

The `usage_threshold` attribute supports:

* `filters` - (Optional) The filters allow limiting the scope of this usage alert. You can only specify up to one filter at this time. See [`usage_threshold.filters`](#usage_threshold.filters) below.
* `gte` - (Required) The value at which this alert will trigger.
* `meter` - (Required) The [Billing Meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/billing/meter) ID whose usage is monitored.
* `recurrence` - (Required) Defines how the alert will behave. Possible values: `one_time`.

<a id="usage_threshold.filters"></a>
### `usage_threshold.filters`

The `usage_threshold.filters` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `customer` - (Optional) Limit the scope of the alert to this customer ID
* `type` - (Required) Possible values: `customer`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a billing alert whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_billing_alert.heavy_usage

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_billing_alert.heavy_usage
```

The billing alert stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a billing alert using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_billing_alert.heavy_usage
  id = "alrt_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_billing_alert.heavy_usage
  identity = {
    id = "alrt_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the billing alert.

Using `terraform import`, import a billing alert using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_billing_alert.heavy_usage alrt_123
```
